operational_simulations.organization: Brazilian supermarket chain with staffed and self-checkout lanes
operational_simulations.bounded_process: resolve produce identification, item-scan mismatch and checkout exceptions
scenarios: visually similar produce, occlusion or damaged packaging
peak-hour queues with camera or scale degradation
operational_simulations.candidate: fine-grained product recognition and scan-mismatch review

operational_simulations.organization: Brazilian grocery retailer with fresh-food departments
operational_simulations.bounded_process: inspect freshness, damage and presentation before replenishment or markdown
scenarios: ambiguous visual defect or mixed maturity
high inbound volume with limited staff and inconsistent lighting

operational_simulations.bounded_process: detect aisle obstruction, spill, unsafe stacking and unattended hazards
scenarios: crowded store with camera blind spots and delayed response
operational_simulations.candidate: video-based hazard detection for human dispatch

technical_hypothesis.interaction_pattern: edge or near-real-time human-reviewed visual alerting
technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: store-specific lighting, camera angle, packaging changes, seasonal produce appearance and intervention-biased review labels can cause severe domain shift and false alerts

training_data.observation_unit: one checkout item event, fresh-item inspection or bounded video hazard window
training_data.input_data: images or short video clips plus SKU, scale, POS, location, timestamp and operating-context fields available at decision time
training_data.target_or_reward: verified item identity or mismatch, audited condition class, or confirmed operational hazard requiring action
training_data.label_source: cashier corrections, quality inspections, incident records and sampled specialist annotation; consistency and coverage are unknown
training_data.prediction_time: before checkout completion, replenishment or markdown decision, or staff hazard dispatch
training_data.class_balance: unknown; material mismatches, defects and hazards are expected to be minority classes
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown across stores, formats, cameras, seasons, packaging and customer-density conditions
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based and store-held-out validation with SKU, season, camera and subgroup slices plus prospective shadow evaluation
training_data.leakage_risks: post-intervention cashier actions, final markdown or disposal codes, incident resolution notes and manually selected exception reason
training_data.representativeness_risks: store format, region, lighting, device, product assortment, packaging, skin tone and mobility-device visibility differ materially
training_data.feedback_loop: alerts change staff attention, customer interaction and recorded outcomes, concentrating future labels on already-detected patterns
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: avoid biometric identification and unnecessary customer profiling; minimize retention, restrict access and assess LGPD purpose, transparency and proportionality
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use barcode and scale validation, controlled produce picklists, scheduled quality inspection, deterministic shelf-life rules, floor walks, incident buttons and human review

portfolio_comparison.reason: shelf-state recognition and retail-loss operations are already represented by RETAIL-001, while item-condition inspection and disposition are represented by RETAIL-002; checkout vision, freshness inspection and store video analytics are also established commercial categories without a distinct uncovered actor, decision and outcome.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt or configure established checkout-vision, shelf and store-operations products where justified; retain deterministic POS, scale, quality and safety controls rather than publishing another generic retail computer-vision opportunity.

research.findings: Brazilian loss evidence remains current, but the repository already covers shelf availability and return-condition vision. Current products and open model platforms cover checkout item recognition, scan mismatch, shelf monitoring and loss-prevention video. Fine-grained SKU retrieval still has precision and domain-shift limits, while biometric or person-focused surveillance raises material LGPD proportionality and transparency concerns.

where_ai_enters.primary_mechanism: recognize fine-grained product, condition or bounded physical hazard patterns from images or short video for human review
where_ai_enters.human_control: store staff retain checkout intervention, quality disposition, markdown, security response, customer interaction and safety decisions
